tested_scope: Exactly two already-durable unique child completion identities C1 and C2, each bound to a stable canonical child key k1<k2. Compare arrival traces [C1,C2] and [C2,C1]. Parent reconstruction deduplicates by completion identity, orders by canonical child key, and then forms an ordered aggregate.
reconstruction_rule: For each trace: build an identity map keyed by completion identity; reject only conflicting duplicate payloads; sort surviving unique completions by stable canonical child key; aggregate in that canonical order.
scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to deterministic reconstruction of one parent aggregate from exactly two already-durable unique child completions with stable canonical keys. No claim for concurrent writers, conflicting duplicate payloads, key collisions, missing child keys, parent processed-state mutation, torn/corrupt writes, more than two children, external side effects, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one adjacent failure case where two durable child completion records use distinct completion identities but collide on the same canonical child key. Verify reconstruction fails closed instead of silently choosing arrival order or overwriting one child. Do not test concurrent writers, parent processed-state mutation, torn writes, more than two child completions, external side effects, or another boundary in that invocation.
